newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-TOP RUSSIAN CLUBS FINED OVER CROWD TROUBLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TOP RUSSIAN CLUBS FINED OVER CROWD TROUBLE.

text.p: Russian champions Spartak Moscow and two other leading premier league clubs have been fined for crowd trouble, league officials said on Wednesday.
Anatoly Grokhovsky, head of the disciplinary committee, said Spartak and Alania Vladikavkaz were each fined 10 million roubles ($2,000) and Torpedo Moscow one million roubles.

CSKA Moscow coach Pavel Sadyrin was hit on the head by a stone during a 1-1 draw with Spartak in last Wednesday's derby in the capital. Alania fans hurled bottles and cans after seeing their side go down 2-1 to Lokomotiv Moscow. Some ran on to the pitch.
"The disciplinary committee warned Spartak and Alania that if anything like this happens again, much more severe sanctions will be applied," Grokhovsky said.
Torpedo were fined after a fan threw a plastic bottle at the referee following their 2-1 home defeat by Zenit St. Petersburg.
